title: Collier County Commission, District 2
what_it_does: County commissioners set the county budget and property-tax (millage) rate, adopt land-use and zoning rules, and oversee county services such as roads, parks, libraries, fire/EMS and utilities.
verified_ballot_note: Cody Davis listed as a qualified candidate for the Nov. 3 ballot (Ballot Brief snippet); party and opponents not verified. District 4 (Daniel Kowal, ~71%) was decided in the August universal primary.

candidates.name: Chris Hall
candidates.occupation: Collier County commissioner since 2022 and current chairman; real-estate investor
candidates.background: Republican incumbent elected in 2022 with more than 70 percent of the vote. His campaign lists fiscal responsibility, workforce housing, constitutional rights, transparency, education and law enforcement as issues and cites priority-based budgeting he says saved the county over $100 million (Sparker's Soapbox candidate summary, 2026). He initially said he would not run again, then changed his mind.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

taxes.summary: At the county's final budget hearing on Sept. 18, 2026 Hall voted with a 3-2 majority to cut the Conservation Collier land-acquisition tax, which let the board reach the rolled-back rate and avoid an increase of about $13 a year for the owner of a home taxed at $400,000. He had proposed reducing the conservation millage at an earlier hearing. All five commissioners then adopted the FY2027 budget of more than $3 billion.

sources.title: Collier's new budget will cut some funding for conservation program

environment.summary: Hall voted on Sept. 18, 2026 to reduce the dedicated tax for Conservation Collier, cutting the land-preservation program's annual collections from about $35 million to about $30 million in order to hold the overall county tax rate down. Commissioners Rick LoCastro and Burt Saunders voted against the cut; Dan Kowal and William McDaniel joined Hall.

sources.title: Collier's new budget will cut some funding for conservation program

record.item: Sept. 18, 2026 final budget hearing: voted with the 3-2 majority to cut about $5 million a year from Conservation Collier's dedicated land-acquisition tax (from roughly $35 million to $30 million a year), reaching the rolled-back property-tax rate; the board then adopted the more than $3 billion FY2027 budget unanimously.
